summary: L-4 ground cab on Kelly Butte, King County WA, dating to 1950; cupola built 1926; restored by volunteers 2008-2011; open only when volunteers staff it, late June to September.

facts.design: L-4 ground cab, 14 by 14 feet, with catwalk (first lookout a 12-by-12-foot cupola cabin)

access.note: Visitors are welcome inside only when a volunteer is on duty; staffed from the end of June to the end of September. Camping is not allowed at the lookout or on its deck.

visit.trail_note: Trail 1031, 1.7 miles with about 1,000 feet of climb from the Kelly Butte Trailhead (Forest Service road 7030, high-clearance vehicle recommended); one trail guide gives 1,100 feet of climb.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register, Forest Service and Snoqualmie association date the first cupola cabin to 1926. A regional history page quotes a 1924 source saying a standard lookout house was completed in December 1924. The current L-4 ground cab is dated 1950 (installation), and the Register calls it a 1932 ground house.
The Register gives 5,409 ft (1,649 m); the Forest Service and TrailChick give about 5,400 ft. The record's 1648.7 m matches the Register.

notes_for_editor: Core history (1926 cupola, 1950 L-4 cab, 1980s last staffing, 2008-2011 restoration, 2012 back in service) is consistent across the Register, Forest Service, Snoqualmie association and TrailChick. Open questions: the 1924 completion date on the Forest Lookouts page conflicts with 1926; the 1932 build date for the L-4 cab comes from the Register alone; the Register's 'staffed until the 1980s' and firelookout.com's 'last staffed in the 1980' do not give an exact year, and the event is recorded as 1980 for sorting only. Current access: Forest Service and association pages say volunteers staff it late June to late September, and the association gives 8 am to 5 pm when staffed; the Register visit reports describe volunteer hosting in summer without giving hours. The Forest Service Enumclaw office phone line (open Wednesdays and Fridays, 9 am to 3 pm) is listed on the Forest Service page but its scope is unclear (office or lookout), so it is not in the story. Trail length and climb: 1.7 miles and 1,000 ft (Snoqualmie, Forest Service) vs 1,100 ft (TrailChick). Forest Lookouts page quotes 1924 source (Six Twenty-Six) without a date for the first build. No photos added; photo licences were not in the text read. Pages read: 7 distinct sources (one failed to produce a usable snippet, the Forest Lookouts page was read with grep only); one web search used. Staffing as_of set to 2026 from a Forest Service page that carries 2026 alerts; the page itself is undated.
